key_insight: RS-JEPA introduces a compact predictive-embedding framework for retrieving matching scenes across different remote sensing sensors without manual labels. Its title highlights scan-path views, but the provided abstract is incomplete and does not explain their implementation or report results.
problem_solved: Finding the same scene across SAR–optical or panchromatic–multispectral imagery despite differences in sensor appearance. Existing self-supervised approaches can focus on sensor-specific pixels, restrict alignment to co-registered image pairs, or require large transformer models.
method: Use a joint-embedding predictive architecture to learn representations for cross-sensor image retrieval.
Incorporate scan-path views, as indicated by the title; construction details are not included in the supplied text.
Adopt a compact framework rather than the large transformers cited in the abstract; exact model size is not provided.
impact: The approach targets label-free retrieval across heterogeneous Earth-observation imagery with a compact model. This could make cross-sensor search more practical, although accuracy and efficiency gains cannot be verified from the supplied excerpt.
visual_elements: Paired SAR and optical images showing the same scene with different sensor appearances.
Conceptual pipeline: sensor images → scan-path views → predictive embeddings → retrieved matches.
Shared embedding-space diagram with matching scenes from different sensors grouped together.
Model-size callout: prior transformers at 118–173M parameters, up to 398M; RS-JEPA size not supplied.
paper_title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
paper_authors: Tanishq Rachamalla, Srishti Kaushik, Muhammad Attique Khan, Gustau Camps-Valls, Swalpa Kumar Roy
